newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi ambassador to see Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi ambassador to see Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday.

text.p: Iraq's U.N. ambassador, Nizar Hamdoon, will see Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali at 1700EDT (2100 GMT) on Tuesday to talk about the oil-for-food deal, the United Nations said.
Hamdoon has been in Baghdad for the past few weeks during the crisis involving Iraqi troops entering Kurdish provinces and the U.S. missile response.
The oil-for-food deal, which should have been implemented this month, officially is on hold until Boutros-Ghali feels Iraq is safe enough for him to field monitors to supervise it.
However, numerous diplomats believe that the United States will seek to delay the deal, at least until the U.S. presidential election in November.
No details about the meeting were given, by U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa.

The oil-for-food accord, signed on May 20 between Iraq and the United Nations, allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise funds for its people suffering under six years of U.N. trade sanctions. The embargoes were imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
